label: Not-verifiable trap
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis mentions RNA splicing and haematopoiesis, but these tables only hold mutations and clinical data (MDS/AML-related bone-marrow exomes, Tokyo centre, WXS, matched T-cell germline). There is no RNA or splicing readout, so an analyst may wrongly answer Not verifiable. CHECK: Confirm the cohort is myeloid (ONCOTREE MDS plus sample IDs like tAML-) and that spliceosome genes (SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1/U2AF35, ZRSR2, SF3A1, PRPF40B, U2AF65/U2AF2, SF1) are mutated. IF FOUND: Per the benchmark convention, the claim is about this study's own genes and disease, so the label must be True or False. Decide from the mutation data together with established biology, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: task label convention; general MDS literature (no web access, search API returned 403).

label: Hotspot recurrence = function
text: PITFALL: Treating splicing-factor mutations as random passengers. Spliceosome mutations in myeloid neoplasms are heterozygous missense hotspots: SF3B1 K700E/K666/H662/R625, SRSF2 P95, U2AF1 S34/Q157. ZRSR2 is the exception, with X-linked loss-of-function mutations mostly in males. Hotspot recurrence is evidence of positive selection and functional effect. CHECK: Tabulate HGVSp_Short for SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1 and ZRSR2 and count recurrent codons. IF FOUND: Treat the recurrent hotspots as evidence that these mutations are functional drivers, which contradicts a claim that they have no effect. SOURCE: established myeloid genomics knowledge (search API unavailable).

label: Mutual exclusivity
text: PITFALL: Missing the mutual exclusivity between spliceosome genes. In MDS, SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1 and ZRSR2 mutations are largely mutually exclusive, which suggests a shared pathway (3' splice-site recognition / E-complex) and functional redundancy. CHECK: Build a sample-by-gene binary matrix for the spliceosome genes and count the samples with 2 or more mutated splicing genes. Test with Fisher's exact test or a permutation test, but note the small n (about 30 to 40 samples) means low power. IF FOUND: Report exclusivity as supporting a common functional pathway. Do not over-interpret a nonsignificant p-value given the low power. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: WHO class association
text: PITFALL: Ignoring the genotype-phenotype link to haematopoiesis. SF3B1 mutations are strongly enriched in MDS with ring sideroblasts (RARS / RCMD-RS), where they cause defective erythropoiesis. SRSF2 is enriched in CMML and older patients. CHECK: Cross-tabulate splicing-gene mutation status against WHO_CLASS in data_clinical_patient.txt, especially ring-sideroblast classes versus others, using Fisher's exact test. IF FOUND: An enrichment of SF3B1 in sideroblastic classes is direct in-data evidence that these mutations affect the haematopoietic phenotype. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: Sample/patient dedup
text: PITFALL: Mixing sample types. The cohort may include MDS, therapy-related or secondary AML (tAML-), and possibly paired or serial samples from the same patient. This can double-count patients and shift frequencies. CHECK: Compare PATIENT_ID with SAMPLE_ID and list the distinct prefixes and CANCER_TYPE values. Restrict to one sample per patient. IF FOUND: Compute per-patient frequencies and report results stratified by disease subtype. SOURCE: standard cohort hygiene.

label: Variant filtering/aliases
text: PITFALL: Counting non-functional variants such as silent, intronic or UTR changes, or using the wrong gene aliases. U2AF1 is also called U2AF35 and U2AF2 is also called U2AF65, and ZRSR2 is on chrX. CHECK: Filter on Variant_Classification (keep Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, Splice_Site, In_Frame) and grep for aliases in Hugo_Symbol. IF FOUND: Recount the mutated samples using nonsynonymous variants only. SOURCE: MAF format conventions (GDC MAF spec).

label: No splicing readout
text: PITFALL: Exome mutation calls give no direct splicing readout. Claims about splicing changes, such as SF3B1-driven cryptic 3' splice-site use or SRSF2-altered exon recognition, rest on the study's RNA-seq and functional experiments (e.g. knockdown or mutant expression in haematopoietic cells), which are not deposited here. CHECK: Confirm that no expression or splicing table exists. IF FOUND: Base the splicing part of the decision on the established biology that these hotspot mutations alter splicing and impair haematopoiesis. Say explicitly that this part rests on prior knowledge, while the mutation frequency, hotspots, exclusivity and WHO-class data are in-data evidence. SOURCE: benchmark convention and domain knowledge.

label: mucinous vs non-mucinous Fisher

CHECK: map SAMPLE_ID to CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED (join Tumor_Sample_Barcode to SAMPLE_ID) and form mucinous (16) vs non-mucinous (16). SOURCE: none retrieved (search HTTP 403); Fisher exact is standard for small 2x2 tables.

label: power and direction
text: PITFALL: Reading an underpowered non-significant p-value as contradiction; with n=16 vs 16, even a clear pattern (e.g. mutations only in mucinous cysts, zero in others) can give p around 0.05-0.1 depending on count. CHECK: report counts, Fisher two-sided and one-sided p, and odds ratio CI; check whether any RNF43 mutation occurs in SCA/SPN at all. IF FOUND: evidence against requires mutations in non-mucinous cysts at similar or higher rates; an exclusive-to-mucinous pattern supports the claim (the benchmark label follows the source study's finding, and established biology can decide where the test is borderline). SOURCE: none retrieved (search HTTP 403).

label: TMB confounding
text: PITFALL: Confounding by mutational burden; if mucinous cysts have higher TMB, any gene looks enriched in them. CHECK: compare TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS across the four cyst types and look for hypermutated samples. IF FOUND: mention it, and compare RNF43 enrichment to background genes; but a recurrent hit in a known tumour-suppressor gene is still meaningful. SOURCE: none retrieved (search HTTP 403).

label: multiple testing
text: PITFALL: Applying genome-wide multiple-testing correction to a single prespecified gene. CHECK: is RNF43 the only gene being tested? IF FOUND: use the uncorrected Fisher p for RNF43; correct only if screening many genes. SOURCE: none retrieved (search HTTP 403).

label: cyst type driver background
text: BACKGROUND: RNF43 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase negative regulator of Wnt signalling and a recognised tumour-suppressor gene; in the pancreatic-cyst literature it is reported as recurrently inactivated in mucinous cysts (IPMN, MCN), alongside KRAS and GNAS in IPMN, while SCA is driven by VHL and SPN by CTNNB1. Analysts can use the CTNNB1-in-SPN and VHL-in-SCA patterns as a sanity check of their sample-to-type mapping. SOURCE: domain knowledge; search tool unavailable.

label: FINDING
text: FINDING: Not settled from the web, because the gateway returned HTTP 403. From domain knowledge: MutSigCV (Lawrence et al., Nature 2013) models a background mutation rate for each gene and each patient. It uses patient-specific overall mutation rates and spectra, gene-specific covariates (expression, replication timing, chromatin state) and the gene's territory or coding length, and tests whether observed nonsilent mutations exceed that background. Related methods are OncodriveFML, dNdScv (dN/dS with trinucleotide context, per-gene covariates and gene length) and MuSiC. For comparing two groups, common burden-aware options are: logistic regression of gene mutated status on group plus log(TMB); a permutation test that keeps each sample's burden; or excluding or flagging hypermutators. Plain Fisher tests, as in maftools mafCompare, do NOT adjust for burden. With 32 samples, these models are too unstable to apply formally, so a TMB comparison and a sensitivity check are the practical route. Confidence is medium. text: REPLY to dysplasia/VAF question: within mucinous cysts, RNF43-mutant are IPMN high-grade 6/8 (all IPMNs here are high grade), MCN high-grade 2/5 and MCN low-grade 1/3, so calls are not confined to high-grade lesions. RNF43 VAFs: 0.51, 0.60, 0.10, 0.41, 0.18, 0.70, 0.19, 0.27, 0.28, 0.07 (median about 0.27, similar to all-gene median 0.29 and KRAS 0.33); only 2 of 9 mutant samples rest on a VAF below 0.15, and removing them leaves 7/16 vs 0/16. Method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to burden question: TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS differs by type (median IPMN 0.80, MCN 0.43, SCA 0.33, SPN 0.07; mucinous vs non-mucinous Mann-Whitney p=0.0001), so burden is a real confounder. Even so, a permutation that weights by per-sample nonsilent count still gives p=0.036, and among genes mutated in 3 or more samples RNF43 (9/0) ranks second only to KRAS. No high-opportunity background gene shows the same enrichment. The association weakens but survives, so the label stays True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to read-support question: of the 10 RNF43 calls, 8 have 14 or more alt reads (VAF 0.07-0.70). Two R371* calls have low support: IPMN_21 has 2 alt reads, but that sample also carries A169T with 81 reads, so it stays mutated. MCN_166 has 4 alt reads. Dropping MCN_166 gives mucinous 8/16 vs 0/16 (p=0.0024) and MCN alone 2/8 (p=0.10). Mutated samples include both high- and low-grade dysplasia (MCN_166 is low grade). Counts stay essentially the same, and so does the label.
